Check that two models are the same model

Source: R/compare.R
pmx_compare.Rd

Simulates both models on one design, each through its own engine, and compares their predictions. This is the check a translation exists to pass: a model read from one format and written to another should predict the same values for the same subjects.

Usage

pmx_compare(
  a,
  b,
  design = pmx_design(),
  tol = 1e-06,
  atol = 1e-09,
  engines = NULL
)

Arguments

a, b

The models to compare: each a model read by a pmx_read_*() function, or a model written by a pmx_write_*() function.

design

A design from pmx_design().

tol

The relative tolerance, a positive number.

atol

The absolute tolerance, a non-negative number.

engines

NULL to choose engines as described above, or a character vector of two engines, "rxode2" or "mrgsolve", for a and b. NA in either place chooses that side's engine as usual.

Value

A zufapmx_comparison, a list with:

pass

TRUE when every prediction agrees.

reason

Why the models could not be compared point by point, or NULL.

worst

A one-row data frame of the worst deviation, or NULL without predictions: the first missing or non-finite prediction, or else the largest relative deviation among points outside atol, or else the largest absolute deviation.

regimens

One row per regimen: the number of points, the number that disagree, the largest absolute and relative deviations, and the reason a regimen was skipped.

predictions

One row per point: regimen, id, time, the two predictions a and b, the deviations abs and rel, and whether it agrees (pass).

engines

The engine and its version for each side.

sides

For each side, how it was simulated, its provenance and the model text the engine ran.

design, tol, atol

The arguments.

Details

Each side runs on an engine (rxode2 or mrgsolve):

  • A written rxode2 or mrgsolve model runs as written, on its own format's engine. That is the text under test.

  • A model, or a written NONMEM model, is written by zufapmx to an engine and runs there: its source format's engine when that is rxode2 or mrgsolve, and rxode2 otherwise.

A side never runs on the engine of the other side's written text, so a translation is never checked by the writer that made it: a compared with pmx_write_rxode2(a) runs a on mrgsolve. engines overrides the choice, including this rule.

Predictions are compared after aligning on regimen, subject and time. A point agrees when its relative deviation is at most tol or its absolute deviation at most atol, which covers predictions near zero. The relative deviation is abs(a - b) / max(abs(a), abs(b)). A missing or non-finite prediction never agrees. Residual error is off.

A comparison that fails is a value, not an error: pass is FALSE and the result says where the models differ. Models that cannot be compared point by point, because their numbers of random effects differ, fail with a reason and no predictions.

See also

pmx_report() writes a comparison as Markdown.

Other comparison: pmx_design(), pmx_report()

Examples

path <- system.file(
  "corpus", "onecmt-oral", "model.ctl",
  package = "zufapmx"
)
model <- pmx_read_nonmem(path)
# Check the NONMEM writer. Both sides run on rxode2, since NONMEM is not
# an engine here; pmx_write_rxode2(model) would run `model` on mrgsolve.
written <- pmx_write_nonmem(model)
cmp <- pmx_compare(model, written, pmx_design(n = 2, regimens = "single"))
cmp
#> <zufapmx comparison> pass
#> a: nonmem model, written to rxode2 by zufapmx, on rxode2 5.1.8
#> b: nonmem text, written to rxode2 by zufapmx, on rxode2 5.1.8
#> Tolerance: relative 1e-06, absolute 1e-09.
#> 0 of 24 predictions disagree.
#> Worst: single, subject 1, time 0.5: 0.77012778 against 0.77012778 (abs 0, rel 0).
#>  regimen points failed max_abs max_rel skipped
#>   single     24      0       0       0
